source_quotes.n_subjects: We report the very first application of thalamic LIFU in three patients with chronic DOC, as part of a first-in-man clinical trial (NCT02522429; UCLA approved IRB #14e001749).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Patients underwent two MR-guided thalamic LIFU sessions one week apart while behavioral assessments using the JFK Coma Recovery ScaleeRevised (CRS-R) [7] were utilized at 12 time points to assess the therapeutic potential of the LIFU procedure.

flags.reason: The paper labels the intensities 'ISPPA.3'/'ISPTA.3' where the figure legend explains '0.3 denotes deration (attenuation) due to absorption by tissue at 0.3 dB/cm-MHz', implying a derating method, but the main text itself does not state the method in the quoted sentence, so in_situ.method is left not_reported and captured only via the figure legend context.
The paper explicitly states assessments were unblinded with respect to the LIFU procedure (e.g. due to visible indicators such as hair removal).

readout_other: JFK Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R), including CRS-R index; vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, blood oxygen) for safety monitoring
direction_notes: Two of three chronic disorders-of-consciousness patients showed clinically significant increases in behavioural responsiveness (including, in one patient, transient emergence from MCS) following thalamic LIFU sessions; the third patient showed no benefit from either exposure.
safety_notes: The intervention was reported as well tolerated and safe: no alteration in vital parameters (blood pressure, heart rate, blood oxygen), no evidence of structural damage, and no other adverse event were noted.

exposures.label: Thalamic LIFU in chronic disorders of consciousness patients

timing.protocol_description: Patients underwent two MR-guided thalamic LIFU sessions one week apart. In each session, sonication was delivered inside the MRI scanner for ten 30-s blocks, separated by 30 s off periods. The transducer focus (55 mm from its surface) was positioned over the left central thalamus using MR guidance.
